idiom_name: hand-written Store<S> over records with a listener list; ViewModel + StateFlow on Android
implementation_notes: Java ships no store, so the realization is a small Store<S> class holding an immutable state object - Java 16+ records (JEP 395) carry actions and states concisely - with dispatch applying a reducer function and subscribe notifying Consumer<S> listeners; List.copyOf and Stream.toList, plus record accessors, keep snapshots from leaking mutable collections. On Android the framework route is a ViewModel exposing LiveData/StateFlow with one-way intent methods, which reproduces the flow without a dispatcher; keep any hand-written store free of Android types so it runs in plain JVM tests. This is why the honest classification is manual: small third-party ports exist but no dominant library provides the structure, and the classic form is justified exactly when the shared state must be replayed or inspected.
pitfalls: A record that holds a mutable List is only shallowly immutable: expose List.copyOf in the accessor, or the previously published snapshot changes retroactively.
Notifying listeners synchronously inside dispatch lets a listener dispatch again, interleaving updates and potentially recursing; queue nested dispatches or document the ordering.
A store kept in a mutable static across Android activities leaks contexts or survives configuration changes with stale UI state; scope it to the application and keep screen state in the ViewModel.
synchronized on the store serialises reads as well as writes; if reads dominate, publish copy-on-write snapshots or a volatile reference instead.
